review_scope: Renderer-backed close-range diagnostic of the project-owned generated raft coating, PFD ripstop, and wetsuit neoprene PBR maps on the current procedural raft and Manny crew fallback.

renderer_evidence.camera_qualification: The guide camera was explicitly activated and assigned as the player-controller view target; the raft and all five crew avatars occupy the review frame.

accepted_findings: All three material families use deterministic 1024x1024 albedo, tangent-space normal, and packed ambient-occlusion/roughness/height maps with wrapped addressing.
The four-way mirrored derivation removes the rejected center-cross seam from the first processing attempt.
The tuned coated-fabric response adds restrained surface breakup to the raft and is acceptable as a project-owned fallback that can transfer to replacement geometry.
The renderer-backed rescue scenario remains functionally successful after import and shader changes.
rejected_findings: The PFD surfaces retain visible high-frequency grain and do not meet a production textile standard.
The blank Manny anatomy, hood-like head treatment, generic wardrobe, and procedural safety-gear silhouettes remain unmistakably placeholder character art.
The raft geometry remains procedural and does not match a scanned or artist-authored production craft at close range.
This diagnostic frame is not approved as photoreal evidence, marketing media, a store screenshot, or final art-direction acceptance.
decision: Keep the maps as an honest project-owned fallback and reusable material foundation. Do not close the M9 photoreal character, raft, PFD, art-direction, or release-media gates. Replace or explicitly approve the geometry and wardrobe through named art review, then repeat the same renderer-backed close-range test.
